author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader sees every specialty with the veterinarians holding it
summary: A read-only page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, shown by first name then last name. All specialties render on one page and the page is reachable only by its own address.
acceptance_criteria: Opening /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows, by its stored name.
Each specialty lists the veterinarians holding it, each shown as first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary").
A specialty no veterinarian holds is listed as held by none, rather than omitted.
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page.
Every specialty appears on the single page and no paging control is offered.
Rendering the page twice yields the same order of specialties, and the same order of veterinarians under each.
No other page of the system links to the specialty directory and no navigation entry names it.
The page carries the same navigation as every other page, to owner search and the veterinarian directory.
Every new piece of user-facing wording on the page is present in each supported language, per REQ-LANG-002.
non_goals: Creating, editing, or deleting veterinarians or specialties through the page (NG-2 unchanged)
Searching or filtering specialties or veterinarians (NG-9 unchanged)
A navigation entry or any inbound link to the page
notes: Grounded in the intake-decision at line 1; no Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. Open question recorded in the PRD: the request states no ordering, so the requirement asks only that the order not vary between renders; the sort key is undecided. A specialty held by no veterinarian is included on the literal reading of "every specialty the clinic knows"; it is shown as held by none, mirroring REQ-VET-001. No new ubiquitous-language term resolved in the intake.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays inside the vet feature package and adds the first read model this codebase has. Two pieces are new ground. First, every specialty the clinic knows is unreachable through VetRepository, because a specialty no veterinarian holds appears in no vet's collection; a new SpecialtyRepository supplies the full list, shaped after PetTypeRepository's explicit name-ordered query. Second, the vet-to-specialty many-to-many is unidirectional, so the page's inverse view is derived in memory by a new value object rather than by adding a mappedBy collection to Specialty. Placing that derivation in a controller would be a fresh breach of the Web controller row of the pattern catalog, which the package-structure section already records as an open gap; the derivation therefore lives in SpecialtyDirectory, a pure function over the two collections and unit-testable without the web layer. The route gets its own SpecialtyController rather than a third mapping on VetController, per the naming rule that a controller is prefixed by the surface it serves. Everything else follows existing pattern: Spring Data repository interface, controller returning a view name, Thymeleaf template under templates/vets reusing the shared layout fragment, message keys in every bundle. Recorded in docs/system-design.md Contracts and in ADR 2026-08-17-specialty-directory-read-model.md. Basis for the code claims is grep over the vet package and the templates (no IDE oracle connected in this dispatch) plus a direct read of Vet, Specialty, VetRepository, VetController, vetList.html, and fragments/layout.html.
integration_points: GET /specialties.html is a new route on a new SpecialtyController in the vet package; it takes no request parameter and no path variable
SpecialtyRepository is a new Spring Data interface over the existing specialties table; no schema or seed-data change is needed
VetRepository.findAll() is reused unchanged and stays served from the existing vets cache; SpecialtyRepository is left uncached, so CacheConfiguration is untouched
The template reuses fragments/layout.html for navigation; layout.html itself is not changed, so no navigation entry names the page
New message keys join all eleven bundles under src/main/resources/messages; existing keys specialties, vets, name and none already carry most of the wording

patterns.description: lookup-entity repository with an explicit name-ordered query; SpecialtyRepository takes the same shape
sorting a specialty collection by name at the read boundary; the directory's specialty order uses the same key
template idiom for this feature: layout fragment, table, first name plus last name, and the none key for an empty collection
Value object row: SpecialtyDirectory and SpecialtyDirectoryEntry are immutable, expose unmodifiable collections, and hold no infrastructure logic

risks.risk: Ordering is an open product question, and an unordered HashSet backs Vet.specialties, so an unsorted render can vary between calls
risks.mitigation: Sort explicitly in SpecialtyDirectory: specialties by name, veterinarians by last name then first name then identity. The identity tiebreak keeps the order total when two veterinarians share a full name. The ADR records these keys as a design choice a product answer supersedes

risks.risk: Reusing the layout fragment with the menu argument 'vets' would mark the veterinarian directory active, implying navigation to this page
risks.mitigation: Pass a menu argument that matches no navigation entry, so no entry is marked active and layout.html gains no new item

risks.risk: The vets cache hands out shared Vet instances; a read model that sorted or mutated the entity's own collection would corrupt cached state
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory copies into its own lists and never mutates a Vet, a Specialty, or a collection it received

risks.risk: REQ-LANG-002 is enforced by I18nPropertiesSyncTest, which walks every file under src/main and compares keys across all eleven bundles
risks.mitigation: Every literal in the new template goes through a message key, and each new key is added to all eleven bundles. Reuse specialties, vets, name and none rather than adding near-duplicate keys

risks.risk: Vet.specialties is eagerly fetched per veterinarian, so reading every veterinarian and every specialty is two unbounded reads per render
risks.mitigation: Accepted at this data scale and unchanged from the existing vet list. The veterinarian read is already cached; revisit only if a requirement introduces a large roster

notes: Design writes: docs/adr/2026-08-17-specialty-directory-read-model.md (new), docs/adr/README.md index row, docs/system-design.md package-structure line, Contracts preamble paragraph, and Contracts rows for SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyDirectory, SpecialtyDirectoryEntry and SpecialtyController, plus REQ-SPECIALTYDIRECTORY-001 added to the Vet, Specialty and VetRepository rows. No design-doc-autofix records exist in this log, so the autofix audit is empty. Open question carried forward, not resolved here: the PRD leaves the list order to product, and the ADR records the sort keys chosen under the narrowest deterministic reading. No new ubiquitous-language term is introduced; SpecialtyDirectory takes its noun from the PRD's own prose, and 'Vet' stays the accepted short form in code.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: SpecialtyDirectoryEntry is a plain value object (two fields, public constructor, no invariant that requires hiding the constructor) but is hand-written as a class with manually reimplemented equals()/hashCode(), duplicating exactly what a record generates. This is the checklist's own rule (code-quality-review skill: 'Records realize the value-object rule ... used for data transfer between pipeline steps') and the codebase already follows it elsewhere for read-model value types. Unlike SpecialtyDirectory (which legitimately needs a class: its canonical construction must stay private behind the sorting `of()` factory, and a public record cannot have a less-accessible canonical constructor than the record itself), SpecialtyDirectoryEntry has no such constraint.
findings.fix: Convert to `public record SpecialtyDirectoryEntry(Specialty specialty, List<Vet> veterinarians)` with a compact constructor doing the same null checks and `List.copyOf`, keeping the custom toString() override. Verify specialtyList.html still resolves `entry.specialty` / `entry.veterinarians`: Spring's ReflectivePropertyAccessor resolves record accessor methods (`specialty()`, `veterinarians()`) as bean-style properties, so the Thymeleaf property expressions keep working unchanged.

approved_aspects: SpecialtyController stays a thin adapter: no business rule, single delegation to SpecialtyDirectory.of(), matching the Web controller row in architecture-principles.md
SpecialtyDirectory's private constructor + static of() factory correctly encapsulates the sort-and-derive invariant; equals/hashCode/toString are consistent with its content
Naming follows the domain vocabulary with no prohibited suffixes (Manager/Helper/Utility/etc.)
Null-safety via Objects.requireNonNull with descriptive messages on every public entry point
Defensive copy (List.copyOf) on the veterinarians list in SpecialtyDirectoryEntry
SpecialtyRepository extends the narrow Repository interface rather than a CRUD base, keeping the read-only page unable to reach a write method, and is annotated @Transactional(readOnly = true)
Comparators are well-documented, including the tie-break-by-id rationale for a total order
Thymeleaf template is simple, uses message keys for i18n (pre-existing keys reused, no untranslated locale gap), and specifies no raw string concatenation
Format check (./gradlew checkFormat) passes clean

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply-chain status for this pass: no NVD match ran. The project configures no OWASP Dependency-Check plugin (build.gradle has no dependencyCheck), and the change set adds no dependency. Framework versions are therefore not verified against the NVD in this review — a human or CI closes that check; it is not a finding against this change.

Non-blocking scale note, no attacker path: SpecialtyDirectory.holdersOf rescans the full veterinarian collection for every specialty, giving O(specialties x veterinarians x specialties-per-vet) work per request on an unauthenticated, unpaged route. At clinic-scale seed data this is negligible and the veterinarian read is cached, so it is not a denial-of-service finding; it would become one only if either collection grew unbounded. Worth an inverted index (group veterinarians by specialty id once) if the dataset ever grows.
approved_aspects: No request-derived input reaches the new handler: /specialties.html takes no path variable, query parameter, or form binding, so the mass-assignment, path-traversal, and cross-request-state rows of docs/security-principles.md are not engaged. No @InitBinder is needed because nothing is request-bound.
Data access is a static JPQL string in SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() with no concatenation and no parameters; the injection-into-data-access row passes.

Least privilege at the persistence boundary: SpecialtyRepository extends Repository rather than a CRUD base, and the query is annotated @Transactional(readOnly = true), so the read-only page cannot reach a write method.

Output escaping intact in src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyList.html: every dynamic value uses th:text (entry.specialty.name, veterinarian first/last name); no th:utext, no inline JavaScript, no Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${...}__), no remote resource loading, and all wording comes from #{...} message keys. The XSS row passes.

Exposed-surface widening is stated and bounded: docs/prd.md REQ-SPECIALTYDIRECTORY-001 and the new ADR name the route, its read-only nature, and the absence of any link to it. The data rendered (specialty names, veterinarian first/last names) is already publicly readable at /vets.html, so the change does not leave the application weaker than the baseline in docs/system-design.md § Security Context.
No secrets introduced: a scan of the full change set for password/secret/token/key/credential patterns returns nothing, and no properties, compose, or manifest file is touched.
No dangerous primitives introduced: no Runtime/ProcessBuilder/exec, no file or stream I/O, no reflection, no serialization annotations, no system /tmp use, no java.util.Random, no System.out/err.

Immutability and null contracts at the boundary: SpecialtyDirectory.of validates both collections with Objects.requireNonNull, SpecialtyDirectoryEntry defensively copies with List.copyOf, and both types expose only unmodifiable state. Derivation is a pure function, so the singleton controller holds no mutable shared state and the read model is thread-safe.
No new dependency is added in the change set, so the four dependency checks in system-design.md § Adding a New Dependency and the plain-HTTP artifact-source prohibition are unaffected.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: PRD acceptance criterion for REQ-SPECIALTYDIRECTORY-001 (docs/prd.md:146) reads 'given every other page of the system, when it is rendered, then none links to the specialty directory.' The only navigation test, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldCarryTheSharedNavigationWithoutAnEntryOfItsOwn, checks that the specialty page itself contains no self-link and no active nav-link — it never renders another page (vetList.html, ownerList.html, welcome) and checks for an absent '/specialties.html' link there. Today the criterion holds only because layout.html was left untouched, a fact no test pins down; a later change that adds a link from another page regresses silently with the current suite green.
findings.fix: Add an assertion to an existing VetController or WelcomeController test (whichever already renders the shared layout) asserting the response body does not contain 'specialties.html', mirroring the not(containsString(...)) idiom already used in SpecialtyControllerTests.

findings.description: SpecialtyDirectoryEntry's hand-written equals()/hashCode() has no direct unit test of its own — it is only ever invoked indirectly through SpecialtyDirectory's list-equality assertions, where the compared instances are always distinct and of the matching type. Jacoco confirms this: the this==other fast path (line 48-49), the not-instanceof branch (line 51-52), and hashCode() (line 58-59) show 0 coverage. This is a real gap in the value type's public contract, but it is likely moot: code-quality-reviewer's line-14 finding on this same round already asks for SpecialtyDirectoryEntry to become a record, which would generate this exact equals/hashCode by the compiler and make hand-testing it unnecessary. Flagging as clarify rather than autofix so the two findings aren't fixed in conflicting directions in the same round.

approved_aspects: SpecialtyDirectoryTests and SpecialtyControllerTests both follow the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} naming school and keep four-phase structure with blank-line separation, no phase comments

Test data follows the three-tier convention: RADIOLOGY/SURGERY and SPECIALTY_HELD_BY_ONE/SPECIALTY_HELD_BY_NONE are named by role, VetFixtures.createASpecialty/createAVet/createAnEntry are anonymous factories with unique-id generation, no bare literals used as mystery values
All construction goes through VetFixtures factories rather than raw constructors, and the factory is reused correctly across both test classes

SpecialtyDirectoryTests is a genuine unit test (no Spring context, no I/O) exercising the real SpecialtyDirectory/Specialty/Vet objects with zero mocking, matching the brief's 'real objects first' rule and improving the pyramid ratio per testing-principles.md § Test Pyramid

SpecialtyControllerTests' use of @MockitoBean on SpecialtyRepository/VetRepository is consistent with the existing VetControllerTests idiom for @WebMvcTest slices — a tolerated pattern under the brief, not a new deviation

Every PRD acceptance criterion except the cross-page non-linking one has direct test coverage, including the two ordering/derivation edge cases (held-by-none specialty kept, vet-holding-none omitted) and the multi-specialty-membership edge case exercised in theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOrderItsEntriesTheSameOnEveryRender
Assertions are fluent AssertJ throughout (containsExactly, isEqualTo on whole objects) with no JUnit assertEquals/assertTrue and no picking apart of individual fields
./gradlew test passes clean for the full suite; Jacoco shows SpecialtyController at 100% line coverage and SpecialtyDirectory at 93%, both comfortably over the 80% brief target
No untrusted external input is parsed by this slice (read-only page, no request parameters), so the fuzz/adversarial-input checklist item does not apply

approved_aspects: The fix delta is three files (docs/prd.md wording, SpecialtyDirectoryEntry converted to a record, one added test in VetControllerTests) and introduces no new trust boundary, no new route, no new input, and no new dependency.

The record conversion preserves both immutability guarantees that the round-1 review relied on. The compact constructor reassigns the parameter (veterinarians = List.copyOf(Objects.requireNonNull(...))), which is the correct record idiom: the defensive copy lands in the generated field, so the generated veterinarians() accessor hands back an unmodifiable list and no caller can mutate the read model after construction. Both Objects.requireNonNull null contracts survive, so the fail-secure construction behaviour is unchanged.

No serialization surface is opened by making the type a record. A grep for SpecialtyDirectoryEntry across src/ shows only SpecialtyDirectory (construction and the entries list), VetFixtures (test), and the Thymeleaf page; the type reaches no Jackson-serialized endpoint, carries no @JsonTypeInfo or other polymorphic-typing annotation, and the JSON /vets endpoint is untouched.

The retained custom toString() exposes only specialty plus veterinarian first/last names — the same publicly readable data already rendered at /vets.html — so it leaks nothing sensitive if it reaches a debug log or an assertion failure. No logging statement was added in the delta.

Template output escaping is unaffected: specialtyList.html is not in the fix delta and the record accessors resolve through the same SpEL property paths, so the th:text-only rendering reviewed and approved in round 1 still holds with no th:utext, no inline JavaScript, and no Thymeleaf preprocessing introduced.

A pattern sweep of the whole fix delta for password/secret/token/credential/api-key strings, Runtime/ProcessBuilder/exec, unsafe Jackson typing (enableDefaultTyping, JsonTypeInfo), system /tmp use, System.out/System.err, java.util.Random, th:utext, and Thymeleaf preprocessing returns no matches.
